title: Blest Instructor! from Thy Ways
description: Blest Instructor! from Thy Ways in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 334 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Freedom from Error, Guilt and Folly”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest In-struc-tor! from thy ways Who can tell how oft he strays? Save from er-ror's growth our mind, Leave not, Lord, one root be-hind.

lines: Who can tell how oft he strays?
Save from error's growth our mind,
Leave not, Lord, one root behind.
Purge us from the guilt that lies
Let us thence, by thee renewed,
Let our tongues, from error free,
Speak the words approved by thee:
While we thus thy name adore,

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
